newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF sees yearly exploration $300-400 mln.
newsitem.headline: YPF sees yearly exploration $300-400 mln.

text.p: Argentine oil firm YPF SA will spend an average $300 million to $400 million a year in exploration from 1996 to 2004, a top firm executive said Monday.

This level of expenditure will be up from $247 million in the period from 1993 to 1995, said Roberto Monti, president of YPF's US subsidiary Maxus Energy Corp, in an address to an conference on hydrocarbon exploration in Argentina.
"It is our belief that there is still a lot of oil and gas to discover in Argentina," said Monti, who has been named YPF's general manager as of April, subject to approval at a shareholders meeting.

But Monti said that the firm sees the average cost of exploration almost doubling to just under $2 per barrel discovered during the period. The rise in costs will come as YPF moves to higher risk prospects, even though Monti said the firm still aims to concentrate on low to medium risk deposits.

Listing YPF's main prospecting areas, Monti said the firm estimates that an extra 500 million barrels of oil and 10 trillion cubic feet of natural gas remain to be found in the Northwest Basin it is exploring on the border with Bolivia.
Building up gas reserves in the Northwest Basin is crucial to YPF's plans to eventually build a gas pipeline to Brazil's industrial heartland of Sao Paulo.

Monti said that the firm has reason to believe it can strike potential reserves of 100 million barrels of oil in the Cuyo Basin and 1.3 billion barrels of oil in the Neuqun Basin and 12 trillion cubic feet of gas. It also hopes to find 300 million barrels of oil onshore in the San Jorge Basin, and another 800 million barrels offshore.
In the Southern Basin in the sub-Antarctic region of Patagonia, YPF feels it can find 300 million barrels of oil and 7.5 trillion cubic feet of gas.
Monti said that the area around the disputed Falkland Islands, which are known in Spanish as the Malvinas, is also promising: "The Malvinas Basin stands out for its area and potential."

Argentina's government reached an agreement with Britain about a framework for allowing exploration in the waters around the Falklands last year. YPF is interested in a joint-venture with British Gas in the area.
Monti said that YPF hopes to find a total 1.5 billion barrels of oil in its offshore Argentine prospects, along with five trillion cubic feet of gas.
YPF has boosted its annual natural gas and output by about 50 percent over the past five years.
